guideSummary.surfnerd: My Khe is a sand-bottomed beachbreak on a long stretch of coast it shares with Non Nuoc, China Beach and Cua Dai. This 30km beach is backed by the verdant Marble Mountains, five isolated limestone outcrops riddled with caves, grottoes, pagodas and shrines. The waves here are on the mellow, below-average side: they break outside at low tide, fill up in the central trough, then reform on the shorebreak sandbars.
guideSummary.surfForecast: My Khe in Da Nang is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf. Winter is the optimum time of year for surfing here. Offshore winds blow from the west with some shelter here from northeast winds. Usually gets local windswells, but groundswells do happen and the optimum wave angle is from the northeast. Waves at the beach break both left and right. It's sometimes crowded here. Surfing here means negotiating dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Nam O Point is a left-hand point breaking over boulders and sand, and it's probably the highest quality wave around. The catch is that it won't switch on until the beaches nearby are maxing out. When it does come to life, it runs fast, steep and shallow, with the left offering more wall than barrel.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Nam O Point in Da Nang is an exposed beach/Jetty break that has reliable surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. Ideal winds are from the west southwest with some shelter here from northeast winds. Waves more likely to be from local windswells than distant groundswells and the ideal wave angle is from the northeast. The beach breaks favour lefts. It's sometimes crowded here. Surfing here means negotiating dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfForecast: Non Nuoc in Da Nang is an exposed beach break that has fairly consistent surf. Winter is the favoured time of year for surfing here. Offshore winds are from the west southwest. Windswells are much more typical than groudswells and the ideal wave direction is from the northeast. The beach breaks offer lefts and rights. When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Surfing here means negotiating dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Binh An is a sandy beach break just north of Da Nang, on Vietnam's central coast. It breaks over sand and offers both lefts and rights, though the waves here tend to be on the smaller side and often lack much shape. For beginners staying in the beachfront resorts, it can serve up mellow crumblers to practise on.

When the surf is up, it can get quite busy in the water. Watch out for dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: China Beach is the surf hub of Da Nang, the same stretch where US soldiers once surfed on R&R. It's a sand-bottom beach break that peels both left and right, and it makes for an easy, welcoming place to paddle out.
guideSummary.surfForecast: China Beach in Da Nang is an exposed beach break that has quite reliable surf. Winter is the optimum time of year for surfing here. Offshore winds blow from the west southwest. Most of the surf comes fis in the form of windswells and the optimum wave angle is from the northeast. The beach break provides left and right handers. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up. Surfing here means negotiating dangerous rips.

guideSummary.surfnerd: Cua Dai Beach is a sand-bottomed beach break near Hoi An that serves up both lefts and rights. A large rivermouth constantly grooms and reshapes the sandbars, so the peaks shift around over time, and the beach has a noticeably steeper slope than nearby China Beach. That same rivermouth pushes fairly polluted water onto this less-developed stretch of coast, which is worth keeping in mind before you paddle out.
guideSummary.surfForecast: Cue Dai Beach in Da Nang is an exposed beach break that has reasonably consistent surf. Winter is the best time of year for surfing here. The best wind direction is from the southwest. Waves more likely to be from local windswells than distant groundswells and the optimum wave angle is from the northeast. The beach break provides left and right handers. Unlikely to be too crowded, even when the surf is up. Dangerous rips are a hazard of surfing here.
